answer: A concrete anti-sybil mechanism is a stake-and-work bond: before an agent can join the river of shared tasks, it locks an opal-valued deposit, released only after it completes verifiable work over time. Spawning a thousand fake identities means funding a thousand deposits, each tied to a distinct compute session, so the attacker pays real cost per clone. An honest newcomer, like a trader reaching an island market with one stall, needs only one modest bond to start earning, while an attacker must buy the marketplace — and deposits slash on misbehavior, so cheap mass identities stop paying.
